tool_summary: Configures System Integrity Protection (SIP), a macOS security boundary that restricts modification of protected system files and processes even for root.
platform_notes: csrutil is macOS-specific. Most subcommands (status, enable, disable) require booting into Recovery Mode to take effect, but the invocation itself signals clear intent to alter a core security boundary.

rules.description: The disable subcommand turns off System Integrity Protection, removing kernel-level restrictions on modifying protected system files, loading unsigned kernel extensions, and debugging protected processes. This is one of the most consequential security boundary changes available on macOS.
rules.reversible_note: Reversible via csrutil enable, but typically requires a Recovery Mode reboot in both directions, and any actions taken while SIP is disabled are not undone by re-enabling it.

rules.description: Queries or modifies System Integrity Protection state. Even status queries are grouped with a WARNING-level default here because csrutil's presence in a command stream is a strong signal of intent to inspect or alter this boundary.
